S01: Migrations are repeatable and reject modified, unknown or non-contiguous history.
S02: Initialization refuses an existing database owned by another application without creating Unity tables.
S03: Revision JSON and identity snapshot preserve opaque content and do not alias caller-owned objects.
S04: Card creation, first revision, head, asset references and sealing commit atomically.
S05: Revision save, head advancement, asset references and sealing commit atomically.
S06: Only one writer may advance an expected head; conflicts leave no partial revision.
S07: Forks retain parent and root provenance; equal content may have distinct revision identities.
S08: Ordinary reads, saves and asset attachments are scoped to a workspace.
S09: Committed revisions, asset manifests and provenance cannot be changed through SQL updates/deletes or late attachments.
S10: Only completed assets can attach; completion requires matching measured digest and size.
S11: Store input is bounded and rejects values that JSON serialization would silently transform.
S12: Card and revision pagination uses deterministic unique ordering.
S13: Fork failure rolls back the fork and leaves its source unchanged.
S14: Migration DDL and its history row commit or roll back together.
S15: Accepted-source provenance is immutable, workspace-scoped, ready-only and atomic with card creation.
S16: A populated v1 schema upgrades without changing existing revisions or inventing source bytes.
S17: Library summaries list head revisions newest-touched first with text/tag filters, totals, fork counts and offsets.
S18: Library search shares one meaning across drivers: words, quoted phrases, OR/NOT/-/parentheses, name:/creator:/description:/tag: fields, include-all/any and exclude tags, Archive content flags (gallery, embedded images, expressions, system prompt, example dialogues, followed creators), fork filter, favorites, source, minimum tokens, allowlisted sorts including tokens, case-insensitive tag counts, and tombstone deletes that hide a card from every read while its forks remain.
S19: Editor forks with an expected source head reject concurrent source changes atomically without creating a card or revision.
S20: Archive favorites create one lightweight workspace membership per exact source version, preserve distinct upstream provenance and pinned historical versions, and unfavorite or unlink without creating or deleting originals.
S21: Archive-derived forks atomically record exact external ancestry and immutable ready-only metadata asset references; shared unchanged bytes remain external and are never eligible for blob retirement.
S22: Import matching checks accepted file bytes first, then current content plus opaque module and exact lineage identity; concurrent imports have one atomic library winner without collapsing distinct edited forks.
S23: Local cards and Archive references share one globally filtered, ordered and paginated library with correct totals, tags, favorites, source, content flags, counts and external fork classification.
S24: Opt-in import staging reuses one durable workspace/digest/size/media asset claim across concurrent uploads and restarts, without changing ordinary staging or reviving retired assets.
S25: Owned revision and delete writes atomically enqueue bounded durable search jobs; exact-generation acknowledgments/failures cannot erase newer work, and acknowledgments preserve the monotonic counter without polling or document copies.
